topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the difficulty and scope of the complement lecture.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental architecture, naming conventions, and central biochemical mechanisms of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinct recognition pathways that detect pathogens and converge to deposit complement on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector functions through which activated complement coordinates pathogen eradication and immune recruitment.

topics.label: Regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from causing damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the pathological consequences and disease presentations resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the molecular mechanisms that pathogens have evolved to avoid complement-mediated clearance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer ends the lecture and previews the next topic in the course.
